ahead: ENDPOINT_HALF.md finds the larger Siegel-model parameter Q=exp((log N)^{1/2}) breaks ENDPOINT_BOUND.md's Section 2 Bonferroni divisor approximation at exactly kappa=1/2: its fixed cutoff m=2*ceil(sqrt(log N)) makes D_0=Z^m blow up from N^{o(1)} to N^{2+o(1)}, so the N^2*D_0*sqrt(Z) term in budget (18) reaches N^{4+o(1)}, exceeding even the trivial O(N^3) bound on E_corr. No retuning of m rescues kappa=1/2 exactly (shown algebraically and numerically); the chain tolerates every fixed kappa<1/2 (open at 1/2), giving E_corr(N) <<_kappa N^3 exp(-c_kappa (log N)^kappa) for every fixed kappa<1/2 -- a family, not a sharp endpoint, mirroring Remark 2.8's own '1/2-epsilon' phrasing rather than Proposition 2.2's original sharp non-epsilon form. Separately, Remark 2.8 itself is an unverified aside in TT's paper (they explicitly decline to carry out the required retuning of their own Proposition 5.2 exponents 3/5,4/5->1/2, 'leaving the details to the interested reader'), so citing the boosted Proposition 2.2 as a black-box input at all is citing an unproved claim, independent of the project-level wall found here. Whoever next works on ENDPOINT_HALF.md or a successor should know: (1) the achievable family kappa<1/2 still does not reach CORRECTED_RH_BRIDGE.md's near-quadratic N^{2+epsilon} target -- that gap is untouched by this whole substitution regardless of how far kappa is pushed; (2) SIEGEL_UNIFORMITY.md's own independent sieve computation (Section 3, level D=N^{1/4}) and LOCALIZED_MIXED_ENERGY.md's kernel machinery both survive fine up to and including kappa=1/2 with no retuning needed, so the wall is localized specifically to ENDPOINT_BOUND.md Section 2's divisor-approximation device, not the whole chain; (3) a genuinely different, non-Bonferroni route to TT's minor-arc/progression control (Proposition 2.2) might avoid this specific wall and reach kappa closer to or at 1/2 -- this was not attempted here and is open work.

work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/ENDPOINT_BOUND.md, Section 2 approximates the Siegel-model sieve weight nu(n) = b_Z * 1_{(n,P(Z))=1} (P(Z) = product of primes p < Z, b_Z = P(Z)/phi(P(Z))) by a bounded-order Mobius truncation B_m(n) = sum_{d | P(Z), d | n, omega(d) <= m} mu(d), with the fixed cutoff m = 2*ceil(sqrt(log N)) and D_0 = Z^m, in order to control the minor-arc supremum of the model exponential sum H(alpha) = sum_{n<=N} a(n) e(n alpha) via Section 4's Type I / character estimates. This device requires D_0 = Z^m to stay N^{o(1)} (so the term N^2 * D_0 * sqrt(Z) in the final budget, equation (18), stays below N^3), while simultaneously needing m large enough relative to H_Z = 1 + log Z (specifically m/H_Z > e in the limit) for the truncation error N * H_Z^{m+1}/(m+1)! to actually decay. hunts/prime_pair_error/ENDPOINT_HALF.md (already on this branch) shows algebraically and numerically (see its artifacts/endpoint_half/check.py) that when Z = exp((log N)^kappa) for kappa >= 1/2, these two requirements become mutually exclusive: any m satisfying the decay requirement forces D_0 >= N^{e+o(1)} with e = 2.71828..., which alone makes N^2 * D_0 * sqrt(Z) exceed N^3. The task: find a way to control the minor-arc supremum of H(alpha) -- equivalently, to prove a bound of the shape of Tao-Teravainen (arXiv:2107.02158v4) Proposition 2.2 equation (2.5), sum_{n in B}(Lambda(n) - Lambda_Siegel(n)) << N exp(-gamma (log N)^{1/2-epsilon}) for arithmetic progressions B, with the larger Siegel-model parameter Q = exp((log N)^{1/2}) -- WITHOUT routing through a bounded-order/Bonferroni Mobius truncation of nu(n) at a fixed cutoff m the way ENDPOINT_BOUND.md Section 2 does. Two live options: (a) adapt Tao-Teravainen's own actual proof of Proposition 2.2 (not their Remark 2.8's unverified sketch) at the larger Q, which per Remark 2.8 requires retuning their Proposition 5.2's exponents 3/5 and 4/5 to 1/2 -- the paper explicitly does not carry this out ('we leave the details of this strengthening to the interested reader'), so this is genuinely open; (b) find a different minor-arc device entirely (e.g. a direct application of TT Lemma 5.1, the fundamental lemma of the sieve, to bound sup_alpha |H(alpha)| on minor arcs the same way hunts/prime_pair_error/SIEGEL_UNIFORMITY.md Section 3 already does for the diagonal/pair-correlation sum B_r(t,h), rather than first replacing nu by a bounded-order truncation B_m and then applying character-sum estimates to B_m). If either succeeds even for exponent kappa strictly between 1/2 and 1/10 (not necessarily reaching sharp 1/2), that already beats the kappa<1/2 family this attempt reached, and should replace ENDPOINT_BOUND.md Section 2 wholesale rather than patching m. If neither succeeds, that is itself worth recording as a second, independent negative result pinning kappa<1/2 as the actual ceiling of this whole proof strategy, not just of the current write-up.
